items.title: Globe at a Glance: From 25 bomb threats over Europe to Putin’s Iran meeting
items.excerpt: FP News Desk| Nov 06, 2026, 06:30:05 IST Bomb threats hit flights across Europe: More than a dozen flights across Europe faced diversions and emergency procedures following a wave of bomb threats. Flights involving Copenhagen, Dublin, Helsinki, Madrid, Milan and Warsaw were among those affected, AP reported. Several aircraft were escorted by fighter jets or searched after landing. Authorities reported no explosives or suspicious materials, with several threats suspected to be hoaxes. Putin meets Iran's security chief: Russian President Vladimir Putin met Iranian security official Mohsen Rezaei at the Kremlin as diplomatic efforts continued to end the US-Iran conflict, Reuters reported. Discussions covered regional security, post-war arrangements and a proposed gas pipeline linking Russia and Iran. Rezaei also conveyed a message from Iran's Supreme Leader. Paraguay president resigns: Paraguayan President Santiago Peña resigned on Thursday following widespread protests triggered by the collapse of digital lender Ueno Bank. The crisis froze millions of dollars in deposits and cost him the backing of his ruling Colorado Party. Minutes after his announcement, the lower house voted 78-0 to impeach him, referring the charges to the Senate. Israel president urges election compromise: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu reiterated claims of foreign interference in last week’s election, despite President Isaac Herzog’s calls for compromise, France 24 reported. Herzog began consultations with party leaders to decide whether Netanyahu or rival Gadi Eisenkot should get the first opportunity to form a government amid deep political divisions. Iran sends nuclear proposal to US through Qatar: Iran has sent a nuclear proposal to the United States through Qatar as diplomatic efforts to end the conflict continue. A senior Iranian official said Tehran would consider discussions only after Washington meets seven demands, including lifting sanctions and releasing frozen Iranian assets, reported by Reuters. The US is reviewing the proposal amid uncertainty over the future of negotiations. The big number: Brent crude dropped 8.7 per cent to $94.62 a barrel, its lowest level in two months, following the Democrats' midterm victory. Investors weighed the possibility of renewed diplomatic efforts to end the Iran war, which has disrupted global energy supplies and pushed up fuel prices, AP reported.

items.title: HT Morning News Brief November 6: Delhi AQI worsens, Trump warns of fresh Iran action and more | India News
items.excerpt: ## Still night, winds from farm-fire belt push Delhi's AQI to 389 Delhi's air got worse through Thursday night. By 7am on Friday, the Central Pollution Control Board's (CPCB) hourly AQI had climbed to 389, 20 points above the 369 in Thursday's 4pm bulletin. The wind near the ground fell almost still, and a layer of warm air held the night's pollution close to the city. Higher up, the wind blew in from the north-west, from Punjab and Haryana, where Nasa's satellite counted 226 farm fires on Thursday. Read the full story here. ## Trump threatens further Iran action but says decision yet to be made The future of the US war in Iran hangs in the balance after Donald Trump and his Republican Party suffered a rout in the midterm elections. But the 81-year-old president has far from wavered from his aggressive rhetoric against Iran. On Thursday (November 5), speaking to reporters at the Oval Office, Trump said that the US is “locked and loaded” to launch a potential operation in Iran, noting that the US military is building more weapons than “we've ever built before.” Full story here. ## Chawri Bazar building collapse: Police flagged unauthorised construction five months before collapse More than five months before Thursday’s deadly collapse of an under-construction building in Chawri Bazar, Delhi Police had written to the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD), flagging unauthorised construction at the property and seeking action by the civic body, documents seen by HT show. MCD acknowledged receiving the communication in a statement on Thursday, saying it had earlier, in April, warned the building’s owner to undertake repairs to ensure structural safety. However, the civic body alleged that the owner used its advisory for repairs as a cover to clandestinely construct an entirely new building. Read the HT report here.

items.title: Gold eases on inflation worries from higher oil; U.S. payrolls data in focus
items.excerpt: Published Fri, Nov 6 2026 12:03 AM EST Updated 28 Min Ago ... Gold prices eased on Friday as a rebound in oil prices fanned inflation worries and bolstered higher-for-longer interest rate expectations, though bullion remained on track for a weekly gain as investors awaited key US payrolls data later in the day. Spot gold Add To Watchlist fell 0.6% to $4,063.39 per ounce by 0248 GMT, but was up 4% so far this week. U.S. gold futures for December delivery Add To Watchlist dropped 1% to $4,072.90. "Crude oil has rebounded mostly over the past day, which remains one of the inflationary knockbacks pressuring gold," said Ilya Spivak, head of global macro at Tastylive. Markets are still digesting the U.S. midterm election outcome, leaving gold largely rangebound in consolidation phase, Spivak said. Oil prices rose more than 1% on Friday but were set for a sharp weekly drop on expectations of a de-escalation in the Iran conflict after the U.S. election result, while persistent Middle East supply concerns continued to support crude prices. Higher energy costs can reinforce expectations that the Federal Reserve will keep interest rates elevated for longer, raising the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding bullion. ... Investors now await the U.S. non-farm payrolls report due at 1330 GMT, with Fed Vice Chair Michelle Bowman also scheduled to speak later in the day. Traders currently see a 68% chance that the Fed will raise rates in December, according to CME's FedWatch tool. On Thursday, two Fed officials made a case for modest and steady rate increases to tackle above-target inflation.

items.title: Hammack Expects Fed Policy to Turn Restrictive as Inflation Stays High | EconoTimes
items.excerpt: By Miriam Hart Nov 6, 2026, 1:43 AM UTC Updated Nov 6, 2026, 1:43 AM UTC 2 min read ... Cleveland Fed President Beth M. Hammack said she expects U.S. monetary policy will need to become restrictive to bring inflation back to 2%, and favors smaller adjustments made more often. At a conference in Zurich on Thursday, Nov. 5, Hammack described inflation pressures as broad-based, with contributions from both supply and demand. She said prices had remained above the Fed’s 2% goal for nearly six years. Her prepared remarks gave no date or size for a future rate move. Hammack said she favored “more frequent smaller adjustments when possible.” She argued that a gradual sequence could limit disruption for households, businesses and financial markets, help the Fed avoid falling behind price pressures and keep high inflation from becoming entrenched. She said the speech reflected her own views, not necessarily those of the Federal Reserve System or her colleagues on the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC). The remarks followed the FOMC’s Oct. 28 vote to hold the federal funds target range at 3.75%-4.00%. The Fed said the committee voted 10-2, with Hammack and Fed Governor Lisa D. Cook dissenting in favor of a 25-basis-point increase. Their votes reflected their preference at that meeting; Hammack did not announce a new committee decision or a future rate path in her speech. September data from the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) showed the personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index rose 3.6% from a year earlier. The index excluding food and energy increased 3.1%. Both readings were above the Fed’s 2% goal. The BEA’s next Personal Income and Outlays report, covering October, is scheduled for Nov. 25 at 8:30 a.m. ET. The next FOMC meeting is scheduled for Dec. 8-9.

items.title: Trump's massive arch wins approval as protesters threaten to block it
items.excerpt: Construction of President Donald Trump's "triumphal arch" in Washington has been given federal approval despite some public opposition. The National Capital Planning Commission (NCPC) voted 8-4 on Thursday to allow construction of the planned 250ft (72m) arch, which the Trump administration has said could begin as early as this week, though legal challenges threaten to block it. Trump appointees on the board said the arch would be a fitting tribute to US history and to veterans. Opponents argue it will block the view of Arlington National Cemetery, the resting place of thousands of US soldiers and servicepeople. Some protesters said they would use their bodies to block any construction. The so-called Arc de Trump - a play on the name of the famous arch in Paris, the Arc de Triomphe - is one of the US president's efforts to remake the capital city in his style and is meant to commemorate the country's 250th anniversary. The approval on Thursday evening came after nearly nine hours of public comment. It is not yet clear when construction of the arch could start, as a number of lawsuits are seeking to block it.

items.title: White House denies Hegseth, Rubio will leave jobs amid Republican election fallout
items.excerpt: The White House has denied rumours that Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth and Secretary of State Marco Rubio might leave their jobs in a post-election shakeup of the Trump administration. US media have reported there are calls to replace Hegseth - in particular over his handling of the Iran war, which is being blamed for heavy Republican election losses. One outgoing congressional Republican has threatened to force an impeachment vote against Hegseth as early as next week. The defence secretary posted a video statement defending his record and denouncing the effort. "You see, they attack me. They attack us because we are effective," he said. "It's not going to work. We will not back down." ## Vance walks Trump tightrope with scathing election critique blaming Iran war Meanwhile, Rubio is denying reports he is considering leaving his post ahead of a 2028 presidential run. Working for Trump until the end of his term has "always been my plan," Rubio told The New York Times in an interview. "I love the work I'm doing," Rubio said. "And plus I always laugh when they say he's going to leave his job. I go, 'Which one?'" The White House and US State Department also shut down reports that Rubio might be leaving after this week's midterm losses, with both calling it "fake news". The defence secretary, though, faces a more uncertain political future. Trump and Vice-President JD Vance have both blamed the Iran war for Republican losses that allowed Democrats full control of the US House of Representatives and the Senate. In a telephone interview with ABC News, Trump said that he had received "calls about" Hegseth, but added that he had "every intention" of keeping him. Later on Thursday, he told reporters at the White House that "Pete Hegseth has done a fantastic job", and went on to list what he sees are some of his achievements, including the arrest of Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro in January and the Iran war, now into its ninth month. The Washington Post reported on Thursday that Trump might be, however, considering ousting General Dan Caine, the chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, or Centcom chief Admiral Brad Cooper. Both played significant roles in offering guidance on the war, which started eight months ago. items.title: Jennie to Release "Someone to Hold" from Netflix Animated Film "Steps" on Nov. 6 - The Asia Business Daily
items.excerpt: by Lee Yiseul Published 06 Nov.2026 10:08(KST) Image from the OST of Netflix animated film "Steps." Courtesy of Netflix. BLACKPINK member Jennie will release "Someone to Hold," a song from the soundtrack of Netflix's animated film "Steps," at 2 p.m. on Nov. 6, her agency OA Entertainment said. "Steps" is an action comedy that retells the fairy tale "Cinderella" from the perspective of her stepsister Lillith. Netflix will release the film on Nov. 20. "Someone to Hold" is a ballad about the bond between sisters and features in the film's climactic scene. The song was written by Justin Tranter, Julia Michaels and Jason Gill. Before its official release, it was nominated in the Best Song for an Animated Film category at this year's Hollywood Music in Media Awards. "I had so much fun working on my first song for an animated film," Jennie said. "I loved the warmth and individuality of the characters, and I was happy to be part of their world, even in a small way." Jennie's collaboration with Tame Impala, "Dracula," spent 23 weeks in the top 10 of the Billboard Hot 100, the U.S. singles chart. In August, she released the digital mini-album "Fallen Angel."

items.title: Russell Brand found guilty of rape and sexual assault | Morning News Bulletin 6 November 2026 | SBS News
items.excerpt: Published 6 November 2026 6:30am Updated 9h ago 6:58am ... British actor and comedian Russell Brand has been found guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault. The offences date back to the height of his fame in the mid-2000's, when he worked for Channel 4 and the BBC. A 2009 sexual assault of a female colleague took place in front of two producers, who told the woman she must give Brand a massage for him to keep working. The woman told a UK court there was a "culture of fear" at Channel 4 at the time around famous actors and the producers did not help her, describing a "culture of fear". In a statement, a spokesperson for Channel 4 said: "Our thoughts are first and foremost with the six women involved in the case against Russell Brand, including those affected by the crimes for which he has been convicted." Brand has been remanded in custody and will be sentenced on Monday. ... It ends a 23-year career that spanned six World Cups and included a European title and the men’s all-time international scoring record. The Portuguese striker had a fallout with coach Jorge Jesus, after leaving the team's training camp without permission.
